## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle AoS components, paired with a list-based respawn intermediate, can approach the streaming ceiling and amortize irregular-append overhead at moderate death rates.

## Layout & approach
The 72 B/particle AoS offers 11 fields per line, but hot loops touch only fractions: loop 1 uses 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot), loop 2 uses 4 of 68 B/p (5% hot), loop 3 uses 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot). The list intermediate adds 4 B/particle for irregular dead-index append. No fusion across the four loops amortizes the dead-byte fraction — 59% dead in hot loops, 95% dead in respawn — so most of every cache-line fetch is wasted.

## Cache saturation
Cost is flat across regimes: at q=0.01, 20.9 ns/p in L1d (N=320) rises to 26.2 ns/p in DRAM (N=10M) — 25% across four transitions, with no sharp knee at L1d spill (N≈455) or L2 spill (N≈7281). A gentle step at L3→DRAM (N≈233016) adds ~1 ns/p. This flatness signals overhead, not bandwidth, dominance. At q=0.1 the DRAM regime degrades more steeply (25.2→31.2 ns/p, N=3100→1M) as list-driven respawn scatter compounds with DRAM latency.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.75–3.51 GB/s is 22–28% of the 12.69 ceiling and 3.7–4.6x above the 5.674 ns/p floor — overhead- and branch-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Against naive scalar it is essentially tied: 0.945x at N=320 (q=0.01), degrading to 1.027x at N=1M; at q=0.1 it reaches 1.172x baseline in DRAM — 17% slower than naive. Against the winner it is 2.7–3.4x slower at q=0.01, narrowing to ~1.9x at q=0.5 but never approaching it.

## Assembly
Loop 1 achieves partial within-particle vectorization: `vmovups` loads 16 B, `vshufps`/`vinsertps` rearrange, `vmulps`/`vaddps` do 4-wide FP — but per-particle, not across particles, so stride-68B fetches a new line each iteration. Only 28/426 insns are vector (6.6%). Death checks use `vucomiss`+`jb` — branchy. Loop 4 (render) is 202 insns/iter, 21 cond branches, `cmovae`×12, with `movzx`+`mov BYTE PTR` byte stores ×16 — entirely scalar. Byte-granular scatters issue partial-line writes that cannot stream, capping bandwidth at ~25% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.945–1.172x of naive (tied or worse) and 1.9–3.4x slower than the winner at every point. At q=0.01, N=320: 0.945x baseline but 2.822x winner; at q=0.1, N=1M: 1.172x baseline — slower than naive. Within-particle vectorization (28 vec insns / 426) cannot compensate for 59% dead-byte fraction, byte-granular render scatter (202 insns/iter), and list-append irregularity. Backend stalls at 59–71% confirm memory-latency-bound, not streaming-bound, behavior.
